# Fired surface inspection rubric

This rubric applies to clear fired production surfaces, including serving tiles. Deliberately textured exhibition swatches use their own display description. Product acceptance is recorded separately from the fact that an observation was made.

## Lighting and position
Inspect against the matte grey board under the fixed bench lamp. Turn the item once and repeat the observation. Record the inspection station code so a second observer can reproduce the viewing setup. A photograph may supplement the entry but does not replace the written grade.

Do not select a grade by comparing a product with a colour nickname. A batch can be rejected even if its appearance resembles a studio swatch. If the surface has removable loose matter, make the separate contamination observation before choosing a defect category.

## Pinholes
For a serving tile, a pinhole with measured mouth diameter at most 0.4 synthetic millimetres goes to rework, provided there are no more than two on the presentation face. Reject a tile with a larger mouth or with three or more pinholes on that face. Record diameter and count; a tiny-hole impression is not a measurement. This section defines grading, not the method or success of rework.

## Silver bloom
On an otherwise clear fired surface, adherent silver bloom covering at most one of the bench grid's sixteen squares goes to rework; coverage above one square causes rejection. Record occupied squares, rounding any partially occupied square upward. Loose residue is not graded as silver bloom until the separate dry-wipe observation distinguishes it from adhered surface change. The named Silver Bloom decorative swatch is unrelated to this criterion.

## Edge chips
An edge chip crossing the marked presentation outline rejects a production tile. A chip wholly outside that outline goes to the rework tray with its location marked on the outline diagram. Do not relabel a chip as a glaze colour variation to avoid recording a disposition.

## Blisters
A raised closed blister on the presentation face rejects the item regardless of its apparent resemblance to a decorative texture. Keep the blister observation distinct from pinholes: an open mouth and a raised closed dome are different recorded features. Record uncertain observations as uncertain for assessor review rather than silently assigning the nearest category.

## Filing and reinspection
Keep the initial grade when an item is reworked. Add a second observation with its own date, station and disposition. Rework is an activity, not automatic acceptance. A second observer can cite the original grid sketch and add a new sketch without overwriting the first.

Separate category counts in the bench ledger. A summary count of rejected pieces must not erase the category and observation that caused a rejection. Any undocumented category remains an explicit gap in the inspection record.
